Chest Press (Machine).description: A machine-based pressing movement for the chest, ideal for beginners.
steps: Sit in the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles at chest level.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the pad as you press.
Press to full extension without forcefully locking your elbows.

Pec Deck.description: A chest isolation machine with swinging handles that targets the pectorals through horizontal adduction.
steps: Sit in the pec deck machine and grip the handles with your arms out to the sides, elbows slightly bent.
Adjust the seat so the handles align with mid-chest height.
Squeeze the handles together in front of your chest.
Hold the contraction briefly at the center.
Return under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your shoulders down and back against the seat.
Avoid letting the handles fly back past a comfortable stretch.
Focus on squeezing your chest rather than pressing with your arms.

Cable Crossover.description: An isolation movement for the chest using cable resistance for constant tension.
steps: Stand between two cable columns with handles attached to high pulleys.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms wide.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Maintain the same elbow bend throughout; do not press the weight.
Step one foot forward for a stable, balanced stance.
Control the stretch; do not let the cables yank your arms back.

Low Cable Fly.description: An isolation movement for the chest using cable resistance for constant tension.
steps: Stand between two cable columns with handles attached to high pulleys.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms wide.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Maintain the same elbow bend throughout; do not press the weight.
Step one foot forward for a stable, balanced stance.
Control the stretch; do not let the cables yank your arms back.

Bench Press (Barbell).description: A compound pushing movement that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with your eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your mid-chest.
Press the bar back up to full arm extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor.
Maintain a slight arch in your lower back.
Drive through your legs for stability.

Incline Bench Press (Barbell).description: A barbell pressing movement on an incline bench targeting the upper chest.
steps: Lie on an incline bench set to 30-45 degrees.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press the bar back up to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades pinched together against the bench.
Lower the bar without bouncing it off your chest.
Keep your feet planted and your glutes on the bench.

Decline Bench Press (Barbell).description: A barbell compound press on a decline bench emphasizing the lower chest.
steps: Set the bench to a decline angle. Lie down and secure your feet.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, then press back up.
Repeat.
tips: Control the descent.
Keep elbows at about 45 degrees to the torso.

Bench Press (Dumbbell).description: A compound chest exercise using dumbbells, allowing a greater range of motion than the barbell bench press.
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended.
Lower them slowly back to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep wrists neutral throughout.
Squeeze your chest at the top of the movement.

Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell).description: An incline pressing movement emphasizing the upper chest.
steps: Set bench to 30-degree incline and sit back with dumbbells at shoulder level.
Press dumbbells up and together until arms are fully extended.
Lower dumbbells back to shoulder level with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.
Press up without banging the dumbbells together at the top.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the bench.

Dumbbell Fly.description: An isolation exercise that stretches and contracts the pectorals through a wide arc of motion.
steps: Lie flat on a bench with dumbbells held above your chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in the elbows, lower the dumbbells out to the sides.
Return to the start by squeezing your chest.
Repeat.
tips: Keep a consistent bend in the elbows throughout.
Do not let the dumbbells go too low.

Bench Press (Smith Machine).description: A bench press variation in the Smith machine, where the guided bar path adds stability for the chest.
steps: Lie on a flat bench set inside a Smith machine.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest.
Pause briefly without bouncing.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Align the bench so the bar lands at mid-chest, not the neck.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down against the bench.
Keep your feet planted and your glutes on the bench.

Incline Bench Press (Smith Machine).description: An incline press in the Smith machine, guiding the bar to target the upper chest and front delts.
steps: Set an incline bench at 30-45 degrees inside a Smith machine.
Lie back and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack and lower the bar to your upper chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Position the bench so the bar lands on the upper chest, not the throat.
Stack your wrists directly above your elbows.
Avoid driving your head forward off the bench as you press.

Push Up.description: A fundamental bodyweight exercise for the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push back up to the starting position.
Keep your body in a straight line throughout.
Repeat.
tips: Tuck your elbows toward your body rather than flaring them out wide.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to prevent sagging hips.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing slightly ahead of your hands.

Chest Dip.description: A compound bodyweight exercise targeting the lower chest and triceps.
steps: Grip parallel dip bars and lift yourself to the top position with arms locked.
Lean your torso forward slightly.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until shoulders are below elbows.
Press back up to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
Bend your knees and cross your ankles to minimize swinging.
Stop the descent if you feel pinching in your shoulders.

Assisted Dip (Machine).description: A beginner-friendly dip performed on an assisted machine that offsets body weight, training the chest and triceps.
steps: Step onto the assisted dip machine with knees on the pad.
Grip the parallel bars and support your weight with straight arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until shoulders are below elbows.
Press back up to the start position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring out wide.
Stop the descent if you feel pinching in the shoulders.
Reduce the assistance gradually as pressing strength improves.

Lat Pulldown.description: A cable machine exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi.
steps: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads.
Grip the wide bar with an overhand grip.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, squeezing your lats.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Drive your elbows down and back rather than pulling with your hands.
Avoid leaning far back or using momentum to move the weight.
Keep your chest lifted and shoulders down away from your ears.

Close Grip Lat Pulldown.description: A lat pulldown variation using a close, parallel-grip handle to emphasize the lower lats and biceps.
steps: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pad.
Grip the close-grip handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Return under control and repeat.
tips: Lean back only slightly, not excessively.
Avoid using momentum to pull the handle down.
Drive your elbows down and back, not just your hands.

Lat Pulldown (Machine).description: A cable machine exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi.
steps: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads.
Grip the wide bar with an overhand grip.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, squeezing your lats.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Drive your elbows down and back rather than pulling with your hands.
Avoid leaning far back or using momentum to move the weight.
Keep your chest lifted and shoulders down away from your ears.

Seated Cable Row.description: A back exercise performed on a cable row machine, pulling a handle toward the torso while seated.
steps: Sit at the cable row station and place your feet on the footrests.
Grip the handle and sit upright with a slight forward lean.
Drive your elbows back and pull the handle toward your lower abdomen.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
Extend your arms under control back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your torso upright with minimal rocking.
Drive your elbows straight back, not out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.

Seated Row (Machine).description: A seated rowing machine exercise with a chest pad that supports the torso, so the lats and the muscles between the shoulder blades do the pulling and the lower back stays out of it. You pull the handles back by driving the elbows behind you, then let them return forward with control.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles sit at lower-chest height, then sit with your chest against the pad and your feet planted.
Reach forward and take the handles with your arms extended and your shoulders relaxed.
Brace your trunk, then pull the handles back by driving your elbows behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull without lifting your chest off the pad.
Pause briefly, then extend your arms to return the handles forward under control.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, keeping your chest on the pad throughout.
tips: Pull with the elbows rather than the hands, so the lats and mid-back lead and the biceps assist.
Keep the chest on the pad and the shoulders down; shrugging or leaning back turns the row into an upper trapezius pull.
Let the shoulder blades spread forward at the start of each repetition to get a full stretch before the next pull.

T-Bar Row.description: A compound row performed straddling a loaded T-bar, building thickness in the lats and rhomboids.
steps: Straddle the loaded T-bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is around 45 degrees.
Grip the handles and keep your back flat.
Pull the bar up toward your chest by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower the bar under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your hips fixed and avoid heaving the torso upright.
Maintain a soft bend in your knees to protect the lower back.
Let the weight stretch your lats fully at the bottom.

Straight Arm Pulldown.description: An isolation exercise for the lats using a cable with arms kept straight.
steps: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attached to the high pulley.
With arms nearly straight, push the bar down in an arc toward your thighs.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Maintain a slight elbow bend without turning the movement into a pressdown.
Hinge slightly at the hips and keep your back flat.
Avoid using body momentum to swing the bar down.

Assisted Pull Up (Machine).description: A machine-assisted pull-up reducing the effective body weight, allowing beginners to train the lats through a full range.
steps: Place your knees on the assisted pull-up machine pad.
Grip the bar with palms facing away, slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Pull your shoulder blades down before bending your arms.
Avoid swinging or using momentum from the knee pad.
Decrease the assistance over time to progress toward unassisted reps.

Pull Up.description: A bodyweight compound pull targeting the lats and biceps.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself under control to a dead hang.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid swinging or kipping.
Engage your lats by pulling your elbows down.

Chin Up.description: A supinated-grip pull-up that strongly activates the biceps alongside the lats.
steps: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Pull yourself up until chin is above the bar.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep the core tight throughout.
Avoid excessive swinging.

Bent Over Row (Barbell).description: A compound pulling movement that targets the upper and middle back.
steps: Hinge at the hips with a slight knee bend.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso at roughly 45 degrees.
Do not use momentum to swing the weight.

Dumbbell Row.description: A unilateral back exercise using a dumbbell for balanced development.
steps: Place one knee and hand on a bench for support.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with arm extended.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, squeezing your shoulder blade.
Lower the dumbbell with control.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: Avoid rotating the torso to hoist the weight higher.
Let your arm extend fully at the bottom for a complete stretch.
Keep your back flat from head to hips throughout the set.

Deadlift (Barbell).description: A full-body compound lift that primarily targets the posterior chain.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot.
Hinge at the hips and grip the bar.
Brace your core and lift by extending hips and knees.
Stand tall at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep the bar close to your body.
Do not round your lower back.

Back Extension.description: An isolation movement targeting the lower back erector spinae on a hyperextension bench.
steps: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench with hips at the pad edge.
Lower your upper body toward the floor.
Raise your torso back up until your body is straight.
Repeat.
tips: Keep movements controlled.
Do not hyperextend beyond neutral spine.

Shrug (Dumbbell).description: A dumbbell shrug targeting the upper trapezius for neck and upper back thickness.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders straight up as high as possible.
Hold briefly, then lower.
Repeat.
tips: Do not roll your shoulders.
Focus on squeezing the traps at the top.

Shrug (Barbell).description: An isolation movement for the upper trapezius.
steps: Stand holding a barbell at arm's length with an overhand grip.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower your shoulders back down with control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid rolling the shoulders forward or backward at the top.
Keep your arms relaxed and let the traps do the work.
Keep your neck neutral instead of jutting the chin forward.

Face Pull.description: A cable exercise targeting the rear deltoids and external rotators.
steps: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends.
Squeeze your rear deltoids and external rotators.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows high, roughly in line with your shoulders.
Choose a light weight and prioritize control over load.
Avoid leaning back or shrugging your shoulders as you pull.

Shoulder Press (Machine).description: A machine-based overhead pressing movement for the shoulders.
steps: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles at shoulder level.
Press the handles overhead until arms are fully extended.
Lower with control to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the pad without overarching.
Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows as you press.

Lateral Raise (Machine).description: A seated lateral raise on a plate-loaded machine, where pads bear against the upper arms so the side deltoids lift the load without the hands gripping it.
steps: Set the seat height so that the pivot of the arm pads lines up with the point of your shoulders when you sit down.
Load the plate horns evenly on both sides and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Place the outside of your upper arms against the pads with your elbows bent and your arms hanging down.
Push out and up against the pads until your upper arms are roughly level with your shoulders.
Lower under control until your arms are back at your sides, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Set the seat first. If the pivot sits below your shoulder the pads drive your arm across your body instead of out to the side, and the side deltoid stops being the muscle doing the work.
Push with the arm, not the hand. The handles are there to stop your arms sliding off the pads -- gripping hard pulls the biceps and forearms into a raise that should be all deltoid.
Stop at shoulder height. Going higher hands the last part of the rep to the traps, and the machine will happily let you.

Reverse Fly (Machine).description: A seated machine exercise for the rear deltoids, also known as the reverse pec deck: facing the pad, you sweep the two handles out and back in a wide arc against the weight stack. The pad keeps the torso still, so the work stays on the back of the shoulders and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height, then sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles with your arms reaching forward and a slight bend in the elbows.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your trunk.
Sweep the handles out and back in a wide arc, leading with the elbows, until your arms are roughly in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly without leaning back off the pad.
Return the handles forward slowly and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Lead with the elbows rather than pulling with the hands, so the rear deltoids do the work and not the biceps.
Keep the chest on the pad and the neck relaxed; leaning back or shrugging moves the load to the upper trapezius.
Choose a weight you can lower under control; a lighter load with a slow return works the rear deltoids better than a heavy swing.

Lateral Raise (Cable).description: A unilateral lateral raise on the cable, providing constant tension on the side delt.
steps: Stand sideways to a low pulley and grip the handle with the hand farther from the machine.
Keep a soft bend in the elbow and let the cable run across the front of your body.
Raise the arm out to the side until parallel to the floor.
Lower under control. Complete reps per side, then switch.
Maintain tension — do not let the weight rest at the bottom.
tips: Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
Pause briefly at the top, do not swing.
Use a lighter load than for dumbbell — cable tension is constant.

Overhead Press (Barbell).description: A compound overhead pressing movement targeting the shoulders and triceps.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bar at collarbone level.
Brace your core and press the bar overhead.
Lock out at the top with the bar over your mid-foot.
Lower the bar back to collarbone height.
Repeat.
tips: Do not lean back excessively.
Squeeze your glutes for stability.

Shoulder Press (Dumbbell).description: An overhead press with dumbbells performed seated or standing, building the front and side delts.
steps: Sit or stand holding dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press both dumbbells overhead until arms are fully extended.
Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to shoulder height.
Do not let the dumbbells drift behind your head.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Stack your wrists directly over your elbows throughout the press.
Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your shoulders rather than flared wide.

Arnold Press.description: An overhead press variation rotating the palms from facing the body to facing forward, working the front and side deltoids.
steps: Hold a pair of dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing you.
Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
Fully extend your arms at the top without locking the elbows.
Reverse the motion and rotate back to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Time the palm rotation evenly throughout the press, not all at once.
Avoid arching your lower back as the weight goes overhead.
Use a lighter load than a standard press to control the rotation.

Lateral Raise (Dumbbell).description: An isolation movement targeting the lateral deltoid for shoulder width.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until arms are parallel to the floor.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Slight bend in the elbows.
Lead with your elbows, not your hands.

Front Raise (Dumbbell).description: An isolation exercise targeting the anterior deltoid through a forward raise motion.
steps: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Raise one or both dumbbells forward to shoulder height.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid using momentum.
Slight elbow bend reduces joint stress.

Rear Delt Fly (Dumbbell).description: An isolation movement targeting the posterior deltoids and upper back.
steps: Hold dumbbells and hinge forward at the hips.
With a slight bend in elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Choose a light weight to keep the movement strict.
Avoid using momentum from the torso to swing the weights up.
Lead with your elbows rather than your hands.

Shoulder Press (Smith Machine).description: A standing overhead press in the Smith machine, with the guided bar path providing stability for the shoulders.
steps: Stand inside a Smith machine with your feet hip-width apart and the bar at shoulder level.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width at shoulder level.
Unrack the bar and press it overhead until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder level under control.
Keep your core tight throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Stand directly under the bar path before unracking.
Tilt your head back slightly as the bar passes your face.
Avoid flaring your ribs as the bar travels overhead.

Upright Row.description: A compound pulling movement for the lateral deltoids and upper traps.
steps: Stand holding a barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Pull the bar straight up along your body toward your chin.
Lead with your elbows, keeping them above your hands.
Lower the bar with control.
Repeat.
tips: Use a lighter weight if you feel pinching in your shoulders.
Avoid bending your wrists excessively as the bar rises.
Avoid swinging or using your legs to heave the weight up.

Bicep Curl (Machine).description: A machine-based bicep curl for isolated arm training.
steps: Sit in the machine and adjust the pad to your arm length.
Grip the handles with an underhand grip.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad throughout the set.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders as you curl.
Extend your arms fully at the bottom without bouncing.

Preacher Curl (Machine).description: A preacher curl performed on a plate-loaded or selectorized machine, locking the elbows on a pad and providing a fixed strength curve.
steps: Sit at a preacher curl machine and adjust the seat so your armpits sit at the top of the pad.
Place the upper arms flat on the pad and grip the handles.
Start with the arms extended — but not locked — at the bottom.
Curl the handles up by flexing the elbows; squeeze hard at the top.
Lower slowly back to the starting position and repeat.
tips: Do not let the elbows lift off the pad at the top.
Stop just short of full extension at the bottom to protect the elbow tendons.

Bicep Curl (Cable).description: A bicep curl using cable resistance for constant tension.
steps: Stand facing a low cable pulley with a straight bar or EZ-bar attachment.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows from drifting forward as you curl.
Straighten your arms fully at the bottom of each rep.
Avoid leaning back to help lift the weight.

Bicep Curl (Barbell).description: A classic biceps isolation exercise using a barbell for maximal loading.
steps: Stand holding a barbell with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid swinging the torso.
Keep elbows pinned at your sides.

EZ Bar Curl.description: An isolation exercise targeting the biceps using an EZ-bar, which reduces wrist strain compared to a straight barbell.
steps: Stand holding an EZ-bar with an underhand grip on the angled portions.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows pinned.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Use the inner or outer grip to vary emphasis.
Keep your wrists neutral on the angled grips.

Bicep Curl (Dumbbell).description: An isolation exercise targeting the biceps.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Avoid swinging the weights.

Hammer Curl.description: A bicep curl variation with a neutral grip targeting the brachioradialis.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing each other.
Curl the weights up while keeping your palms facing inward.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides throughout.
Keep your wrists straight and rigid throughout the curl.
Avoid leaning back or swinging the weights up.

Incline Curl (Dumbbell).description: A bicep curl on an incline bench for a deeper stretch of the long head.
steps: Sit on an incline bench set to 45 degrees, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Let your arms hang straight down with palms forward.
Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders against the bench throughout.
Don't let your elbows drift forward as you curl.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders forward as you lift the weight.

Concentration Curl.description: An isolation curl performed seated for peak bicep contraction.
steps: Sit on a bench with legs spread, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Brace your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Lower with control.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: Keep your upper arm vertical and let only the forearm move.
Avoid swinging your torso to help the weight up.
Match the reps on each arm to avoid muscle imbalances.

Preacher Curl (EZ Bar).description: A curl variation using a preacher bench to isolate the biceps.
steps: Sit at a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad.
Hold an EZ-bar with an underhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control until arms are nearly straight.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid bouncing at the bottom to protect the biceps tendon.
Keep your wrists neutral rather than letting them bend back.
Don't shrug your shoulders as the bar rises.

Tricep Pushdown.description: An isolation exercise targeting the triceps using a cable machine.
steps: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment.
Grip the bar and pin your elbows to your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Only your forearms should move.

Tricep Rope Pushdown.description: An isolation exercise targeting the triceps using a cable machine.
steps: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment.
Grip the bar and pin your elbows to your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Only your forearms should move.

Overhead Tricep Extension (Cable).description: A cable triceps exercise: facing away from the weight stack, you hold a rope behind your head and straighten your elbows to push it up and overhead. The overhead position stretches the long head of the triceps, and the cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole movement.
steps: Attach a rope to the low pulley and select a light weight.
Take the rope in both hands, turn away from the stack and step forward into a staggered stance so the cable pulls you back.
Raise the rope overhead with your elbows bent and your upper arms close to your ears, so your hands are behind your head.
Brace your trunk and keep your upper arms still, then straighten your elbows to push the rope up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Pause briefly at the top, then bend your elbows to lower the rope back behind your head under control.
Repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows pointing forward and the upper arms still; letting them flare out or drift turns the extension into a press.
Step far enough forward that the cable holds you steady, and avoid arching your lower back as the arms go overhead.
Use a weight you can control through the full stretch; heavy loads pull the elbows apart.

Tricep Extension (Machine).description: A seated machine isolation exercise in which the upper arms stay supported on a pad while the elbows extend against two handles, loading the triceps along a fixed path without help from the shoulders or torso.
steps: Sit in the tricep extension machine with your back against the seat pad and your upper arms resting flat on the arm pad in front of your chest.
Take a handle in each hand with your elbows bent and your hands up near shoulder height.
Keeping your upper arms pressed into the pad, extend your elbows to drive the handles down and away until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your triceps at full extension, then bend your elbows to return to the start under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Set the seat height so your upper arms lie flat on the pad and your elbows line up with the machine's pivot — that alignment is what keeps the work on the triceps.
Keep your upper arms glued to the pad; letting them lift turns the movement into a press and takes the triceps out of it.
Straighten your arms fully without snapping the elbows, and resist on the way back instead of letting the weight stack drop.

Seated Dip (Machine).description: A selectorized machine version of the dip: seated upright with your back against the pad, you press two lever arms down by your sides until your arms are straight. The movement follows the path of a bodyweight dip, but the load is the weight you select on the stack, and the seat takes your body weight.
steps: Select your weight on the stack and adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height when you are seated.
Sit upright with your back against the pad and grip the handles at your sides with your elbows bent.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest up, then press the handles down by straightening your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, with your arms straight but not locked out hard.
Let the handles rise back up under control until your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, keeping your back against the pad.
tips: Keep the elbows close to your sides so the work stays on the triceps.
Do not let the shoulders roll forward or shrug as the handles rise; stop where the stretch in the chest and shoulders is comfortable.
Keep your back against the pad; leaning forward shifts the work toward the chest.

Skull Crusher.description: A lying triceps extension using a barbell to isolate the triceps through a full range of motion.
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell over your chest with a narrow grip.
Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending at the elbows.
Extend your arms back to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep upper arms vertical throughout.
Lower slowly to protect the elbows.

Close Grip Bench Press.description: A bench press variation with a narrow grip that shifts the emphasis to the triceps.
steps: Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell with hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower the bar to your lower chest keeping elbows close to your sides.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: Keep elbows tucked to maximize triceps activation.
Avoid too-narrow a grip to prevent wrist strain.

Overhead Tricep Extension (Dumbbell).description: An overhead triceps extension with a dumbbell in each hand, both arms working together.
steps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended overhead.
Lower the dumbbells behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the starting position.
Keep your elbows close to your head.
Repeat for the planned number of reps.
tips: Move only your forearms, keeping the upper arms still.
Brace your core to avoid arching your lower back.
Choose a weight light enough to reach a full stretch.

Tricep Kickback.description: An isolation exercise for the triceps performed in a bent-over position with a dumbbell in each hand.
steps: Hinge forward at the hips, holding a dumbbell in each hand with the elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Extend both arms straight back, squeezing the triceps.
Hold briefly at full extension.
Lower with control.
Repeat for the planned number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your sides and finish with your arms in line with your torso.
Use light dumbbells and avoid swinging them with momentum.
Keep your back flat and your knees slightly bent to hold the hinge.

Bench Dip.description: A bodyweight pressing movement with hands on a bench behind the body, emphasizing the triceps.
steps: Sit on a bench and place your hands on the edge beside your hips.
Slide your hips off the bench with legs extended.
Lower your body by bending your elbows to 90 degrees.
Press through your palms to return to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your hips close to the bench as you lower.
Avoid letting your shoulders roll forward at the bottom.
Bend your knees to make the movement easier.

Wrist Curl.description: A dumbbell wrist curl that isolates the forearm flexors and trains both arms independently.
steps: Sit on a bench with the forearm resting on the thigh, palm up.
Hold a dumbbell with the wrist hanging off the knee.
Let the dumbbell roll down to the fingertips.
Curl the dumbbell up by flexing the wrist.
Lower under control. Complete reps per side.
tips: Move only at the wrist — keep the forearm still.
Roll the dumbbell to the fingertips for full range.
Train both arms with the same load and reps.

Reverse Curl.description: A barbell curl with an overhand grip targeting the brachialis and forearm extensors.
steps: Stand and hold a barbell with an overhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep wrists straight.
Move through a full range of motion.

Farmer's Walk.description: This full-body exercise involves walking while holding heavy dumbbells, effectively building grip strength, core stability, and overall muscular endurance.
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended at your sides.
Retract your shoulder blades and brace your core, maintaining a neutral spine.
Walk slowly and deliberately for a set distance or duration, taking short, controlled steps.
Keep your chest up and avoid leaning to one side as you walk.
Focus on maintaining a strong, stable posture throughout the movement.
tips: Use the heaviest dumbbells you can control without compromising form.
Breathe deeply and rhythmically to maintain core tension.
Imagine you are balancing a glass of water on your head.

Leg Press.description: A machine-based compound movement for the quads and glutes.
steps: Sit in the leg press machine with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety catches and lower the platform by bending your knees.
Push the platform back up until legs are nearly straight.
Do not lock your knees at the top.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back and hips pressed into the seat.
Lower only as far as you can without your hips tucking under.
Drive evenly through your whole foot, not just your toes.

Leg Extension.description: An isolation exercise for the quadriceps using a machine.
steps: Sit in the leg extension machine with ankles behind the pad.
Extend your legs until they are straight.
Squeeze your quads at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Adjust the seat so your knees align with the machine's pivot point.
Keep your back pressed against the pad throughout.
Avoid swinging the weight up with momentum.

Hack Squat.description: A compound lower-body machine exercise on the hack squat sled, targeting the quadriceps through a guided squat pattern.
steps: Load the hack squat machine and step on, positioning your back and shoulders against the pads.
Place your feet shoulder-width on the platform with toes turned out slightly.
Unlock the safety handles and lower the sled by bending at the knees and hips.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Drive through your heels to extend the legs and push the sled back to the start.
Re-engage the safety handles after your final rep.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed against the pad throughout the movement.
Placing the feet higher on the platform shifts emphasis to the glutes and hamstrings.
Control the descent; do not bounce out of the bottom position.

Squat (Smith Machine).description: A squat performed on the Smith machine, using the fixed bar path for added stability while training quads and glutes.
steps: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height and step under it.
Position the bar across your upper traps and unrack it.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, slightly forward of the bar.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Brace your core and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Set the safety stops just below your lowest squat depth.

Squat (Barbell).description: A compound lower-body movement targeting the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings.
steps: Position the bar on your upper traps.
Unrack and step back, feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and squat down until thighs are parallel.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.

Front Squat.description: A barbell squat with the bar held in front on the deltoids, emphasizing quads and core.
steps: Clean or rack the bar to your front deltoids with elbows high.
Squat down keeping torso upright until thighs are parallel.
Drive back up.
Repeat.
tips: Maintain high elbows to keep the bar stable.
A more upright torso increases quad activation.

Goblet Squat.description: A beginner-friendly squat with a kettlebell held at chest height for improved posture and depth.
steps: Hold a kettlebell at chest height with both hands.
Squat down keeping the weight close to your chest.
Drive back up.
Repeat.
tips: The goblet position naturally encourages an upright torso.
Push knees out at the bottom.

Bulgarian Split Squat.description: A single-leg squat variation with the rear foot elevated.
steps: Stand in front of a bench, place one foot behind you on the bench.
Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand back up.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Track your front knee over your toes without letting it cave inward.
Square your hips forward and avoid rotating toward the bench.

Lunge (Dumbbell).description: A unilateral lower-body exercise with dumbbells targeting quads and glutes through a stepping motion.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward with one foot and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push off the front foot to return.
Alternate legs.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Front knee should track over your toes.

Walking Lunge.description: A traveling lunge stepping forward leg over leg, training the quads and glutes with an added balance challenge.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on hips.
Step one foot forward into a long lunge.
Lower until both knees are around 90 degrees.
Drive through the front heel and step the back foot forward.
Continue alternating legs as you walk forward.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lower until both knees reach about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright as you step.
Drive through your front heel to step forward smoothly.

Seated Leg Curl.description: A machine isolation exercise for the hamstrings performed in a seated position, providing consistent tension and reduced hip flexor involvement compared to the lying variant.
steps: Adjust the seat back and ankle pad so your knees align with the machine's pivot point.
Sit upright, place the backs of your ankles on top of the pad, and grip the handles.
Curl your lower legs down and back under the seat as far as the machine allows.
Pause at peak contraction, then return the weight slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Keep your back firmly against the backrest throughout the movement.
Point toes slightly toward your shins at peak contraction to increase hamstring activation.
Control the eccentric phase — do not let the weight pull your legs back quickly.

Lying Leg Curl.description: An isolation exercise for the hamstrings using a leg curl machine.
steps: Lie face down on the leg curl machine with ankles under the pad.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the bench throughout the set.
Avoid jerking the weight up with your lower back.
Use a full range of motion without letting the stack slam down.

Romanian Deadlift (Barbell).description: A hip-hinge movement emphasizing the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Stand holding a barbell at hip level with an overhand grip.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back while keeping legs nearly straight.
Lower the bar along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding the lower back.
Maintain the same slight knee bend for the entire rep.
Go only as deep as your hamstring flexibility allows.

Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbell).description: A hip-hinge movement with dumbbells and soft knees, loading the hamstrings and glutes through a controlled stretch.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs with a soft knee bend.
Hinge at the hips and push your glutes back.
Lower the dumbbells along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Keep your back flat and shoulders pulled back.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your knee angle constant; the movement is a hinge, not a squat.
Tuck your chin slightly to keep your spine in one straight line.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning backward.

Good Morning.description: A hip-hinge movement with a barbell on the back for posterior chain development.
steps: Stand with a barbell across your upper back.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back while keeping your back flat.
Lower your torso until it's nearly parallel to the floor.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat.
tips: Start with a light bar and master the hinge first.
Keep a soft bend in your knees throughout.
Stop the descent if your lower back starts to round.

Hip Thrust (Machine).description: A machine hip thrust performed on a plate-loaded glute drive, where the built-in back pad and foot platform set the position so the hips can extend against the load without setting up a bench.
steps: Load the plate horns evenly and sit into the machine with your upper back against the pad and your feet flat on the platform.
Pull the hip pad or lap bar across your hips and adjust it so it sits on the crease of the hips, not on your stomach.
Set your feet so that your shins will be roughly vertical when your hips are at the top, and take hold of the handles.
Drive your hips up by squeezing the glutes until your thighs are level with your torso, and hold briefly at the top.
Lower under control until your hips are just short of the bottom of the range, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Get the pad on the hip crease. Sitting it up on the stomach is the only genuinely uncomfortable thing this machine does, and it is fixed by moving the pad, not by adding padding.
Finish with the hips, not the lower back. If the ribs flare at the top you have run out of hip extension and started arching, which is where the machine stops training the glutes.
This is the hip thrust to reach for when the bench and barbell are taken -- the back pad and platform are part of the frame, so there is no setup to get wrong.

Hip Thrust (Barbell).description: A compound glute exercise using a barbell across the hips.
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, barbell across your hips.
Drive your hips up until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips back down with control.
Repeat.
tips: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down at the top.
Finish with your shins vertical, driving through your heels.
Reach full hip extension without arching your lower back.

Hip Abduction (Machine).description: A machine exercise targeting the outer hip muscles.
steps: Sit in the hip abduction machine with pads against your outer thighs.
Push your legs apart against the resistance.
Hold briefly at the widest point.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat.
tips: Sit tall and keep your back against the pad.
Don't let the weight stack slam down between reps.
Choose a resistance that allows a full range of motion.

Hip Adduction (Machine).description: A machine exercise pressing the legs together against resistance, isolating and strengthening the inner-thigh adductors.
steps: Sit on the hip adduction machine with your back against the pad.
Place your legs against the pads with the machine set to a comfortable stretch.
Squeeze your legs together until the pads meet in the middle.
Hold the squeeze briefly in the fully closed position.
Let your legs open back out under control to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Choose a start width that stretches without straining your groin.
Move through the whole range at an even, controlled speed.
Do not let the weight stack slam down as your legs open back out.

Cable Kickback.description: A cable isolation exercise for the glutes, extending the hip back against constant resistance.
steps: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and fasten it around one ankle.
Stand facing the machine, holding the frame lightly for balance, and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
Kick the cuffed leg straight back, extending the hip fully while keeping the knee nearly straight.
Squeeze the glute at full hip extension, then return the foot slowly to the start.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
tips: Lead with the heel to maximize glute activation over hamstrings.
Keep the hips square; avoid rotating the pelvis as the leg kicks back.
The movement comes entirely from the hip — keep the back and torso still.

Kettlebell Swing.description: An explosive hip-hinge movement using a kettlebell for power and conditioning.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor in front.
Hinge at the hips, grip the kettlebell, and hike it back between your legs.
Explosively drive your hips forward to swing the kettlebell to chest height.
Let the kettlebell swing back between your legs.
Repeat in a fluid motion.
tips: Power the swing with your hips, not your arms or shoulders.
Treat it as a hinge, not a squat, with minimal knee bend.
Finish each rep standing tall with glutes squeezed and core tight.

Standing Calf Raise (Machine).description: A standing machine exercise isolating the calves through a full stretch and rise onto the toes.
steps: Stand in the calf raise machine with the balls of your feet on the platform.
Position the shoulder pads firmly.
Lower your heels below the platform for a full stretch.
Push through the balls of your feet to rise onto your toes.
Squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees straight but not locked throughout the movement.
Pause briefly in the stretched position instead of bouncing.
Avoid cutting the range of motion short as fatigue sets in.

Seated Calf Raise.description: A machine calf raise performed seated to specifically target the soleus muscle.
steps: Sit at a calf raise machine with the pads resting on your thighs.
Lower your heels as far as possible.
Raise up onto your toes.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: The bent knee slackens the gastrocnemius, so the soleus does more of the work.
Use a full range of motion.

Calf Raise (Smith Machine).description: A standing calf raise in the Smith machine with the bar held behind the thighs at arm's length, the guided bar keeping the movement steady.
steps: Stand in the Smith machine with your back to the bar, set just below hip height.
Reach back and grip the bar behind your thighs with both hands, arms straight.
Unrack the bar and raise up onto the balls of your feet.
Squeeze your calves hard at the top.
Lower your heels to the floor under control (below the edge if you stand on a low platform).
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid bouncing out of the bottom stretch position.
Keep your knees straight but not forcefully locked.
Use a slow tempo through the full range rather than pumping short reps.

Ab Crunch (Machine).description: An abdominal isolation exercise performed on a seated machine that flexes the spine against resistance.
steps: Sit in the abdominal crunch machine and grip the handles.
Position the chest pad against your upper body.
Contract your abs to crunch your torso forward and down.
Squeeze at the bottom of the movement.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Initiate the movement with your abs, not your arms.
Exhale as you crunch forward.
Avoid using momentum by rocking your body.

Cable Crunch.description: A kneeling abdominal exercise flexing the spine against cable resistance, allowing progressive loading of the rectus abdominis.
steps: Kneel in front of a cable machine with a rope attachment at the top.
Hold the rope near your forehead with elbows bent.
Crunch down by flexing your spine and bringing your elbows to your thighs.
Squeeze your abs hard at the bottom.
Return to the start position and repeat.
tips: Avoid pulling the rope down with your arms.
Keep your hips fixed so movement comes from the spine.
Exhale fully as you crunch down.

Hanging Leg Raise.description: An advanced core exercise performed hanging from a bar.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip.
Raise your legs in front of you until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
Avoid swinging.
Repeat.
tips: Curl your pelvis up at the top to fully engage your abs.
Keep your shoulders engaged rather than hanging passively.
Bend your knees to make the movement easier if needed.

Captain's Chair Leg Raise.description: A bodyweight core exercise on a captain's chair that targets the lower abs and hip flexors with straight legs for greater difficulty.
steps: Position yourself in the captain's chair with your back flat against the pad and forearms on the armrests.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them until parallel with the floor or higher.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Keep your legs as straight as possible throughout.
Avoid swinging — control the movement with your core.
For less difficulty, bend the knees slightly.

Crunch.description: A basic abdominal exercise focusing on the rectus abdominis.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and hands behind your head.
Curl your upper body toward your knees, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor.
Squeeze your abs at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
Exhale as you curl up and inhale on the way down.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.

Plank.description: An isometric core exercise that strengthens the entire midsection.
steps: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs back and rise onto your toes.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Lower your knees to exit the hold.
tips: Do not let your hips sag or pike up.
Squeeze your glutes and quads.

Russian Twist.description: A rotational core exercise targeting the obliques.
steps: Sit on the floor with knees bent, lean back slightly.
Hold your hands together or hold a weight at chest level.
Rotate your torso to one side, then the other.
Keep your core braced throughout.
Repeat.
tips: Rotate from the torso rather than just swinging the arms.
Keep your chest lifted and your spine long as you twist.
Move at a controlled tempo instead of racing through reps.

Ab Wheel.description: A core exercise rolling a wheel forward and back, training anti-extension of the spine.
steps: Kneel on the floor and grip the ab wheel handles shoulder-width.
Brace the core hard so the lower back stays neutral.
Roll the wheel slowly forward, extending the body as far as you can control.
Stop before the hips sag or the back arches.
Pull the wheel back to the knees by contracting the abs.
tips: Brace the core before each rep — do not let the lower back arch.
Build range gradually, stopping short of any hip sag.
Drop to a wall stop if you cannot control the bottom.
